skill.name: web-performance
skill.description: Diagnoses browser loading, Core Web Vitals, main-thread work, and layout/paint bottlenecks. Use for a slow page or measured browser-performance issue; isolated React renders and GPU passes have specialist workflows.
skill.summary: Use measured browser data to prioritize loading, interaction, layout, and animation performance improvements.
skill.author: shreyam1008

content.value_statement: Slow loading and delayed interactions require different fixes, and laboratory scores can hide real user problems. This skill guides measurement and targeted browser performance improvements.
actual_capabilities: Explain LCP, INP, and CLS targets using the 75th percentile of field visits, segmented by mobile and desktop.
Recommend loading improvements for JavaScript bundles, critical resources, responsive images, fonts, and server-rendered content.
Guide browser trace analysis for long tasks, forced layouts, dropped frames, and dominant rendering costs.
Recommend responsive work scheduling through task chunking, yielding, idle callbacks, and Web Workers.
Provide an animation-loop example with elapsed-time handling, capped time steps, and hidden-tab timing reset.
Apply a triage checklist covering resource discovery, animation scheduling, layout batching, long tasks, and media sizing.
limitations: The skill provides written guidance, not an automated audit runner or bundled measurement tools.
Diagnosis requires application context, browser traces, or field measurements supplied through available tools.
Isolated React rendering and detailed GPU optimization require specialist workflows beyond this guidance.
Browser API support varies, and field data may be unavailable; laboratory results do not prove healthy field metrics.

use_cases.title: Improve Storefront Loading
use_cases.description: Prioritize the measured LCP resource and reduce blocking scripts, oversized images, and font delays on product pages.

use_cases.title: Investigate Slow Interactions
use_cases.description: Use interaction traces to separate input delay, handler work, and presentation delay before selecting targeted fixes.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Browser Animation
use_cases.description: Review animation scheduling, layout reads and writes, and frame timing across display refresh rates.

prompt_templates.title: Understand My Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these LCP, INP, and CLS measurements: [measurements]. Explain the targets and identify what additional field or laboratory evidence is needed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of available performance measurements

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Loading Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this loading trace and resource waterfall: [evidence]. Identify the LCP resource, blocking work, and three prioritized changes with validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate diagnosis of slow initial loading

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Interaction Delays
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this interaction trace: [trace]. Separate input delay, handler work, and presentation delay. Recommend measured fixes and supported scheduling fallbacks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced investigation of poor interaction responsiveness

prompt_templates.title: Review Runtime Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this animation loop and traces: [evidence]. Compare 60Hz and 120Hz budgets, layout batching, worker opportunities, and GPU constraints. Define regression checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance review across devices and refresh rates

output_examples.input: My product page has field LCP of 3.4 seconds. The waterfall shows the hero image is discovered late.
output: LCP exceeds the 2.5-second target. Confirm this value represents the 75th percentile for the relevant device segment.
Investigate earlier discovery of the measured hero image and appropriate fetch priority. Preload only if evidence shows critical late discovery.
Compare loading traces after the change and monitor field LCP separately from laboratory results.

output_examples.input: My animation stutters. The trace shows geometry reads after style writes, and the loop assumes 60Hz.
output: Batch DOM geometry reads before writes to reduce forced synchronous layout.
Schedule visual updates with requestAnimationFrame and use timestamps rather than assuming a fixed display refresh rate.
Verify transform and opacity behavior in a trace, then compare dropped frames at 60Hz and 120Hz.

best_practices: Measure the dominant loading or runtime cost before making changes, then repeat the same measurement after each fix.
Evaluate field metrics at the 75th percentile and separate mobile, desktop, and laboratory results.
Feature-detect scheduling APIs and test representative devices, refresh rates, and GPU conditions.
anti_patterns: Treating one fast Lighthouse run as proof of healthy field Core Web Vitals.
Preloading many resources without confirming their importance to the measured critical path.
Changing renderers or applying workers and WebAssembly without evidence that they address the dominant bottleneck.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers browser loading, Core Web Vitals, interaction responsiveness, layout work, and animation timing.

faq.question: Does it run an automatic performance audit?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and a checklist; browser tools or supplied measurements are needed for diagnosis.

faq.question: Which measurements should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide field LCP, INP, and CLS when available, plus loading waterfalls or interaction traces relevant to the reported problem.

faq.question: Is Lighthouse enough to validate improvements?
faq.answer: No. Laboratory runs help diagnose problems, but field metrics must be evaluated separately at the 75th percentile.

faq.question: Does it handle React and GPU bottlenecks?
faq.answer: It helps identify browser-level costs. Isolated React rendering and detailed GPU optimization need specialist workflows.

faq.question: Are scheduling APIs supported everywhere?
faq.answer: Support varies. Feature-detect scheduler APIs and retain appropriate fallbacks; reserve idle callbacks for deferrable work.
